interest: Military moves against party government after the February 26 Incident, and 70th Diet laws.
overview: This file from U.S. State Department decimal file 894.03 documents political, constitutional, and legislative developments concerning the Japanese Imperial Diet between late 1934 and mid-1937, with a primary focus on the period from October 1936 through May 1937. Key despatches from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo, written by Chargé d'Affaires Erle R. Dickover and Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, analyze contentious proposals emerging from military circles following the February 26 Incident to drastically curtail the powers of the Diet and bar political party members from holding cabinet portfolios. The records detail the intense political friction between the army and established political parties, Prime Minister Kōki Hirota's mediation, and the War Ministry's public retreat in the face of widespread public backlash. In addition, the file contains extensive documentation on the legislative output of the turbulent 70th Diet session under Prime Minister Senjūrō Hayashi—including major taxation hikes, defense budgeting, state economic monopolies, and social welfare programs—as well as an earlier 1934 military intelligence report outlining the factional composition and party affiliations of both houses of the Diet.

subfiles.summary: This detailed report recounts the political turbulence of the 70th Diet, including the fall of the Hirota cabinet, the formation of the Hayashi cabinet, repeated prorogations, and the abrupt dissolution of the House of Representatives. It outlines the national budget of 2.81 billion yen and analyzes thirty-nine specific laws encompassing drastic tax revisions, national bond authorizations, and social welfare programs like the Mothers and Children Protection Law. In addition, the legislation establishes strategic economic controls such as alcohol monopolies, gasoline blending mandates, silk stabilization, and funding for colonial administration in Korea, Saghalien, and Manchuria.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 2403: '48 Laws Passed by 70th Session of Imperial Diet'
